spec_match.rationale: Reproduces the exact §3.1.6 role mappings (navigation/link vs tablist/tab/tabpanel), the §3.1.9 activation-focus split (native anchor focus-start-point move vs focus retained on the tab), automatic activation on arrow-key focus as the spec describes, and the tree-pruning behavior via hidden panels — explicitly labelled as the semantic target, not ::scroll-marker output.

interactive.rationale: Two fully keyboard-operable widgets (native anchors + scrolling pane; WAI-ARIA tabs with roving tabindex, ArrowLeft/Right/Up/Down with wrap, Home/End), park-focus buttons for guided comparison, and a shared focus journal recording every real focusin event.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index promises hand-built reference implementations of both patterns with a live focus journal, which is what the page is.

edge_cases.rationale: Wrap-around, Home/End, scroll-position-driven aria-current, and the automatic-activation divergence are covered and disclosed; not covered is a disabled-tab or vertical-orientation variant, which the CSS feature itself does not model either.

references.rationale: Links chromestatus.com/feature/5109685301673984, the §3.1.9 activation anchor, the WAI-ARIA APG tabs pattern, and both sibling concepts.

conformance.rationale: The feature-level suite covers the parse contracts this page contextualises; the behavioral contracts it demonstrates are hand-built equivalents and are not claimed as browser conformance, which is the honest boundary.

runtime_evidence.rationale: CDP keyboard drive on headless Chromium 141.0.7390.37: park → Tab lands on tab-one; ArrowRight selects tab-two with panels [hidden,visible,hidden]; End→tab-three, Home→tab-one; Tab from the active tab lands on panel-one (role=tabpanel); links half click on #lk-two updates aria-current to [false,true,false], scrolls the pane (scrollTop 176) and the journal logged section#lk-two receiving native focus; zero console errors; desktop screenshot read.

telemetry_health.rationale: Asserts a11y-page-init, every tab-selected index, and every links-activated hash via showcaseTelemetry, with demo-telemetry.js deferred.

design_system.rationale: All colours from CSS variables, selected/current states use the black-on-ivory inversion, tab and link targets set background with color, focus-visible outlines in accent-blue, comparison table scrolls in its own container.

accessibility.rationale: This page is the accessibility demonstration: correct roles/aria-selected/aria-controls/aria-current, roving tabindex verified by keyboard, focusable panels, labelled nav and tablist, aria-live activation notes, and kbd-annotated instructions.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Verified at 1280×2200 (screenshot read: both halves side by side, unclipped) and CDP-emulated 360×740 DPR3 touch where the pair stacks single-column: scrollWidth 360, no horizontal overflow, all targets ≥44px (screenshot read).

openQuestions.title: Add a native-vs-reference comparison once a 154 build is verifiable
openQuestions.detail: When the verification environment has Chrome 154 (or Canary with CSSScrollMarkerGroupModes), place a real scroll-marker carousel in tabs mode beside the hand-built tablist and journal both, so visitors can see the native focusgroup reproduce the reference behavior stop-for-stop. Kept out now because on 141 the native half would not differ between modes, which would blur the page's honest framing.

guidanceConsulted.query: accessible tablist roving tabindex arrow key keyboard interaction
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Match ARIA implementations to actual behavior — role=tab requires the full keyboard contract; prefer native elements; verify with the accessibility tree.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Tabs are native buttons carrying role=tab with the complete APG keyboard contract (roving tabindex, arrows with wrap, Home/End, Tab into panel); the links half uses plain nav + anchors with no ARIA beyond aria-current; behavior verified by CDP keyboard drive.

guidanceConsulted.query: accessible tablist roving tabindex arrow key keyboard interaction
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use native interactive elements and focus management primitives rather than scripted div widgets.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Both halves are built from button/a/nav/section with tabindex only where the pattern requires it (-1 roving, 0 on panels, -1 on fragment targets so native anchor focus works).

summary: The strongest angle for a semantics-only feature: both target patterns built honestly and driven end-to-end by keyboard under CDP, with the focus journal making the one-stop-vs-N-stops difference measurable in any browser. Explicitly separated from ::scroll-marker output so nothing is claimed for 141 that 141 does not do.
